result.question:
I'm worried that urgent work on Transformer 1 at site MAIN is stuck behind an overloaded technician. Give me the MAIN site's work order KPIs for the last 6 months, including backlog, overdue count and average completion time. Then list every open work order on Transformer 1 with its number, description, priority, scheduled date and assigned technician, and flag which ones are overdue.

For each technician assigned to those work orders, count how many open work orders they currently hold at MAIN. Anyone holding more than 5 counts as overloaded.

Next, work out TDCG from the latest oil sample using hydrogen, methane, ethane, ethylene, acetylene and co only. Use these limits: Condition 1 up to 720 ppm, Condition 2 from 721 to 1920, Condition 3 from 1921 to 4630, and Condition 4 above 4630.

If Transformer 1 is at Condition 2 or higher, do the following for any overdue work order on it that sits with an overloaded technician. Reassign it to the technician with the fewest open work orders at MAIN, choosing among those who have worked on Transformer 1 before and are not overloaded. Give it a start date within the next 7 days that avoids any day with 3 or more scheduled work orders at MAIN. If it is Condition 1, don't reassign anything. Just list the overdue items and recommend a catch-up order, ranked by priority and then by how late they are.

If every technician with Transformer 1 history is overloaded, don't reassign. Tell me who is least loaded and recommend bringing in outside help. If any of the six gases is null in the latest sample, use its most recent non-null value and flag it as carried forward.
result.answer:
I didn't reassign anything. Transformer 1 is at DGA Condition 4, but no work order on it has a technician assigned, so no one can be overloaded.

**MAIN work order KPIs, last 6 months**
- Total: 3; completed: 0
- Backlog: 3
- Overdue: 0
- Average completion time: 0 hours. This isn't a real average: nothing has been completed, so there's nothing to average.
- Priorities: one each at P1, P2 and P3. All 3 work orders are on Transformer 1.

**Open work orders on Transformer 1**
| WO | Description | Priority | Status | Scheduled date | Technician | Overdue? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1000051 | OLTC inspection: on-load tap changer (suspected contact wear/coking) | 1 | WAPPR | None set | None | No* |
| 1000053 | Corrective oil work (oil treatment/degassing/filtration, internal inspection) | 2 | WAPPR | None set | None | No |
| 1000052 | Oil sample retest (DGA) and insulation check (thermal fault) | 3 | APPR | None set (notes say target 2026-10-01) | None | No |

*1000051's notes give a target start of 2024-01-19, which passed more than 2.5 years ago. That date is only in the description text, not in a schedule field, so the system doesn't count it as overdue. It's also still waiting for approval.

**Technician workload**
- None of these work orders has a technician, so there were no workloads to count and no one is overloaded.
- No technician has any recorded work on Transformer 1. If you want to reassign later, there's no in-house candidate with history on this unit.

**TDCG from the latest oil sample (2024-01-19)**
All six gases were present, so nothing was carried forward.
- Hydrogen 2,850 + methane 7,400 + ethane 5,470 + ethylene 16,650 + acetylene 7 + CO 32 = **32,409 ppm**
- That puts it at **Condition 4**, far above the 4,630 ppm limit.
- The sample is over 2.5 years old, so current gas levels are unknown.

**What this means**
Your worry about an overloaded technician doesn't match the data. The urgent work isn't stuck behind anyone. It's stuck because nobody has been assigned and two of the three work orders haven't been approved. Given Condition 4, I recommend:
1. Approve 1000051 (P1) and 1000053 (P2) now.
2. Assign technicians and set start dates for all three. Do the P1 first (OLTC inspection), then the P2 (oil treatment), then the P3 (DGA retest, targeted for 2026-10-01).
3. No one in-house has worked on Transformer 1, so consider bringing in an outside transformer specialist. You'll also need a new oil sample, because the last one is from January 2024.
